title: Ada and the Archive Revisited
premise: Odile Whitlock smuggles stolen memories in sealed canisters past the orbital customs ring of Meridian Station, funding a quiet life tending a navigation beacon whose original commission records have been erased. When a ghost ship's manifest surfaces bearing Odile's birth name — a name they buried decades ago — they discover the beacon is actually a dormant archive of the war's true origins, and someone has finally found the key. Hunted by both the Concord navy and the insurgent Choir who each want the archive silenced or weaponized, Odile must decide whether to broadcast the truth, which will end the war by exposing their own family as its architects. In the end, Odile transmits the archive at the cost of their anonymity and their ship, choosing a known self over a safe one.
about_author: Gideon Marchetti is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent eleven years writing technical manuals for deep-space relay stations before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write about people who keep systems running that no one wants to look at too closely.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Odile runs a routine smuggling pass through customs, hiding memory canisters in coolant drums, then tends the ancient beacon on the station's dark side. Third-person limited POV. Establishes Odile's competence, loneliness, and the quiet dread of a life built on erasure.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: A broker friend, Teodor, shows Odile a corrupted manifest listing the Halcyon Vane — decommissioned before launch — with 'E. Whitlock' as registered courier. Odile's hands shake; that name died with their mother. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the past knocking on a door they welded shut.

chapters.title: Coolant and Contraband
chapters.summary: Odile investigates the manifest's source while maintaining cover with customs officer Ilsa Reyes, who suspects them but plays a long game. Flashback fragments surface unbidden — a childhood on the Halcyon Vane. POV: Odile. Beat: paranoia tightening like a pressure seal.

chapters.title: The Choir Sings in Numbers
chapters.summary: Insurgent agent Wren Solano makes contact, claiming the beacon broadcasts a cipher only the Choir can read, and offers protection for 'cooperation.' Odile refuses but doesn't report her. POV: alternating Odile/Wren. Beat: two predators circling the same prey.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile pries open the beacon's maintenance shell and finds an archive core older than the war itself, keyed to Whitlock biometrics. It hums awake at their touch. POV: Odile. Beat: awe curdling into horror — the beacon was waiting for them.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Reyes confronts Odile privately: she's tracked the manifest anomaly too, and Concord Command wants the beacon seized within days. She offers a blind eye if Odile walks away. POV: Reyes. Beat: unexpected sympathy from an enemy; temptation of escape.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: The archive partially unlocks, playing a recorded memory: Odile's mother, an archive architect, sealing away proof that the Concord manufactured the war's opening attack. POV: Odile, deep in recovered memory. Beat: identity cracking — their inheritance is complicity.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the Choir plans to broadcast doctored archive data framing Concord leadership to seize power. She needs Odile's biometric key. POV: Wren. Beat: chilling clarity that neither side wants truth, only leverage.

chapters.title: Seventeen Canisters
chapters.summary: Odile weighs selling everything and fleeing, loading their smuggling ship one last time. A near-miss customs sweep forces them to jettison cargo — including, unknowingly, a tracker planted by the Choir. POV: Odile. Beat: grief for the life they're already losing.

chapters.title: The Tracker Blooms
chapters.summary: Concord marines raid the beacon following the tracker's signal; Odile escapes through maintenance shafts as the archive chamber is sealed behind them. Reyes covers their exit, burning her career. POV: alternating. Beat: betrayal, sacrifice, no way back.

chapters.title: Dark Side Run
chapters.summary: Odile drifts in a crippled shuttle, rationing air, replaying mother's memories for warmth and strategy. They realize the archive needs a transmitter array — the Halcyon Vane's wreck, still orbiting beyond the debris belt. POV: Odile. Beat: despair transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Teodor's Price
chapters.summary: Teodor agrees to ferry Odile to the wreck but demands the archive's commercial memory cache as payment — a fortune in blackmailed secrets. Odile pays, hating what it makes them. POV: Teodor. Beat: complicity; everyone profits from hidden things.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Halcyon Vane
chapters.summary: Boarding the derelict, Odile walks the corridors of their erased childhood, finding the transmitter intact and a final message from their mother: the truth must be given freely, never sold. POV: Odile. Beat: mourning and reconciliation with a dead parent.

chapters.title: Choir Ascendant
chapters.summary: Wren's fleet arrives at the debris belt; the Choir seizes the wreck and tortures Teodor for Odile's location. Wren, uneasy, delays the worst of it. POV: Wren. Beat: the corrupting weight of command; Wren begins to doubt the cause she serves.

chapters.title: Two Keys
chapters.summary: Captured aboard the wreck, Odile bargains: the archive requires living Whitlock consent at the console, so Wren needs them alive and willing. Stalemate in a dead ship's bridge. POV: Odile. Beat: power inverted — the powerless holding the only key.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: In forced proximity, Wren confesses the Choir purged her own village's records; she joined to recover them and became what she hated. Odile shows her a fragment of true archive data. POV: Wren. Beat: empathy across enemy lines; seeds of defection.

chapters.title: Concord Arrives
chapters.summary: A Concord battle group jumps into the system, intent on vaporizing the wreck and the archive with it. Reyes, now disgraced, sends Odile a warning on an open channel — her last act of faith. POV: Reyes. Beat: the cost of conscience made explicit.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Debris Belt
chapters.summary: With minutes before bombardment, Odile must give consent at the console while Wren holds off her own mutinous officers. The transmitter spools up; the archive verifies Odile's identity against forty-year-old biometric ghosts. POV: Odile. Beat: terror and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Odile consents, and the full archive floods every receiver in the system: the manufactured attack, the names, the Whitlock signature on the founding lie. The Concord fleet hesitates mid-burn. POV: omniscient over the system. Beat: catharsis — truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Ceasefire spreads station by station as soldiers on both sides receive the same memories. Wren arrests her own commanders; the Choir fractures between truth-seekers and opportunists. POV: Wren. Beat: victory that feels like loss; institutions don't die cleanly.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Odile, publicly revealed and stripped of every alias, faces a tribunal that cannot decide whether they are hero or heir to villains. They claim the name E. Whitlock aloud for the first time. POV: Odile. Beat: claiming identity as an act of courage, not comfort.

chapters.title: Beacon, Relit
chapters.summary: Months later, Odile returns to the dark side of Meridian, recommissioning the beacon openly as a public archive of the war. Reyes visits; Wren sends word from the new armistice council. Odile signs the log with their real name. POV: Odile. Beat: quiet resolution — visibility chosen, memory kept honest.
